title: The gerund: two actions at the same time

sections.content: You know the gerund (*gerundio*) from B1 Unit 2: it shows actions that happen together. The gerund (*llevando*, *pidiendo*, *documentando*) says how or while the main action happened, and it has the same subject as the main verb. It is a good way to describe a protest: the people did one thing and, at the same time, another.

items.spanish: Las Madres caminaban alrededor de la plaza llevando un pañuelo blanco.
items.english: The Mothers walked around the square wearing a white headscarf.

items.spanish: Pedían información sobre sus hijos marchando cada jueves.
items.english: They asked for information about their children, marching every Thursday.

items.spanish: La Vicaría ayudaba a las familias documentando los casos.
items.english: The Vicaría helped the families by documenting the cases.

items.spanish: Los exiliados hablaban de la represión publicando informes.
items.english: The exiles spoke about the repression by publishing reports.

sections.content: The gerund never changes for gender or number: *llevando* for one person or for many. It is not a second finite verb: *marchaban pidiendo*, not *marchaban pidieron*.
